analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation edit to docs/architecture/inference.md. It adds one table row near head line 1090 describing prompt-chunk attention: 128-query blocks, a fused causal prefill path for eligible head_dims, and the kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0. The supplied units are head-text lines 1-796 of the document, which are unchanged context; the changed line 1090 falls outside the supplied text but is visible in the patch excerpt. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key-handling, wire-protocol or cache-storage behavior changes in this PR.

The row refers to an attention-kernel selection change that lives in MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/AttentionV1.swift and Paged/PagedLayerCache.swift. Those files are not supplied here, so this review cannot confirm that the fused causal path preserves per-request isolation, masking or numerical equivalence. I treat that as an unverified contract, not a finding.

The nearby text describes the prefix cache, SSD tier and Nemotron slot. It touches T-041 (prefix-cache oracle and at-rest artifacts), but nothing in the changed row alters cache scope, the TTL, the HMAC lookup tags or the KEK handling. Any threat-model update would depend on the unseen kernel-level change; the doc line alone does not show one.

No security regressions or threat-model gaps identified from the supplied evidence. If a companion code PR changes attention masking in prefill, a reviewer should verify that the fused .causal path cannot leak across sequences in a batch or across cache scopes.
